rationale: The urinary trial with extra-virgin oil as a comparator ended with no posted results. An unrelated saw-palmetto paper and registry disagree about their placebo. Parkinson diet-pattern cohorts use broad urinary measures without an isolated oil exposure. The enriched-oil prostate pilot reports an inconclusive aggregate symptom comparison. Urgency frequency after culinary extra-virgin oil remains unresolved.

A short Parkinson caffeine trial favored caffeine on a secondary bradykinesia subscore. Limb-only and longer motor comparisons were inconclusive, and a caffeine preprint reports faster progression. Two actual brewed-tea animal experiments differ on exploratory crossings and do not measure bradykinesia. A weak short-term constituent inference remains plausible without a verified brewed-tea comparison.

A randomized thyroid biopsy trial found less procedural anxiety after dark chocolate, alongside the earlier favorable open-label student trial. A masked chronic-fatigue crossover had favorable within-period anxiety data with unequal starting medians and no paired treatment contrast. A healthy snack trial was inconclusive. Expectancy, different anxiety settings and no Parkinson anxiety comparison support only a weak lean against worsening.
